Alex: Heads up — on the long-running stream test (8k->32k) I’m seeing steady memory drift on Mistral variants, ~+2.1% per 1k extra tokens.
Maya: Is that the usual fragmentation pattern or something new with rope scaling?
Alex: Looks rope-related. When sequence length crosses certain boundaries, page allocations spike and we don’t compact/reuse as expected.
Li: Can you paste the alloc trace from the profiler?
Alex: Sure — shortened: \n```
kv_pages_allocated=4120 -> 5584 after crossing 16k
page_frag_ratio=0.28 -> 0.46
kv_reuse_hits=0.12
heap_delta_per_1k=+2.1%\n```

Samir: Interesting. Does it differ between GQA vs MQA mode?
Alex: Yes. In GQA runs reuse hits are lower; MQA shows slightly better contiguous allocation but more frequent small-page churn.
Maya: That maps to what we hypothesized — GQA's key/value partitioning prevents some page-coalescing heuristics.
Li: Any correlation with kernel selection? Maybe the kernel switch for long seqlen forces different alignment
Alex: Good call. When runtime switches to the ’long-attn-tiling’ kernel we see a rebase in kv slot indexing which invalidates a couple of free-list entries.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: perf-test/long-stream-2026 started by Alex at 1899991200
Samir: Can you attach a minimal repro? even a short script that hits the 16k boundary with repeated prefix updates.
Alex: Pushed gist: https://gist.redwood/kv-drift-repro (short script + config). Repro steps in the gist.
Maya: I ran repro on a local GPU (A10) — confirmed. Also saw that continuous batching increases the effect: coalesced batches hold onto partial KV pages longer.
Li: So batching heuristics + kernel switch + GQA partitioning -> poor free-list reuse. Sounds like 3-way interaction.
Samir: Could we fix by flushing small free pages into a per-seqlen slab instead of leaving them in global free-list?
Maya: Per-seqlen slab might be good. Also consider a lightweight compaction pass on seqlen transition.
Alex: Prototype compaction: on seqlen transition, scan free-list for pages with >50% fragmentation and try to merge. Quick test reduced leak slope to near-zero for MQA, ~0.3%/1k for GQA.
Li: Do we have perf impact numbers for compaction? any latency spikes?
Alex: Minimal — compaction is amortized across the transition window. P50 unchanged, P95 +12ms in worst-case for a single transition.
Samir: Acceptable trade for most customers. For latency-sensitive routes maybe make it opt-in via config.
Maya: Also think about kernel-selection policy: prefer kernels that preserve page alignment at transition, if available.
Li: Agree. Runtime could prefer the kernel with alignment-preserving allocator when sequential growth is predicted.
Alex: I’ll open a draft PR with three parts: (1) opt-in compaction pass on seqlen crossing, (2) per-seqlen slab allocator, (3) kernel-selection hint for allocator alignment.
Samir: Make sure to add unit tests that simulate interleaved small and large prefixes to catch regressions.
Maya: And add a perf-test matrix entry for MQA vs GQA vs plain to track differences over time.
Alex: Will do. Also logging: add small telemetry metric kv_reuse_rate_by_model_variant so we can monitor in prod.
InfraBot: perf-test/long-stream-2026 completed: failure=0 duration=23m
Li: Nice. Thanks Alex — that repro script is gold.
Samir: TL;DR — root cause is allocator/free-list interaction with kernel switch + batching heuristics; mitigation = compaction + per-seqlen slabs + kernel hint. Follow-up PR + perf test.
Maya: Adding you all to the RFC thread so we can track design decisions. :thumbsup:
Alex: Thanks — will circle back with PR link and perf numbers.
